hints: How can you check whether writing all numbers from 1 through x uses any digit more than n times?
Count each digit by place value; zero needs special treatment because leading zeroes are not written.
The check is monotone in x, so binary-search the largest feasible x.
analogy: Imagine ten counters, one per key: writing another number can only increase the counters.
example: For n=5, writing 1 through 12 uses five ones; 13 would use a sixth, so the answer is 12.
algorithm: For a candidate x, count occurrences of every digit in 1..x using high, current, and low parts at each decimal place, subtracting leading zeroes for digit 0. Binary-search the largest x whose ten counts are all at most n. Use 10n+1 as an infeasible upper bound: the numbers ending in 1 already use that key n+1 times. Use wide integer arithmetic for powers and counts.
correctness: Every place-value count includes exactly the written digits at that position. Since extending the list never decreases any count, binary search finds the last feasible endpoint.
complexity: O((log U)^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space, for a safe upper bound U on the answer.
